canaries.overview: The Canary Islands offer a massive variety of volcanic trails, from the ancient laurel forests of Tenerife and La Gomera to the deep calderas of La Palma. The standout day hike is the 12,188-foot summit of Mount Teide, reached via a steep climb or a cable car to the upper slopes, though the final push requires an advance permit. Walkers can find everything from easy coastal paths to steep ridge scrambles across the archipelago.

months.4: Temperatures begin to rise slightly, making coastal trails warmer while the high volcanic ridges remain perfectly comfortable for long day hikes.
months.7: Midsummer heat makes exposed coastal and low-altitude trails demanding. The best walking is found above 6,000 feet or in the dense, cloud-draped laurel forests where temperatures stay mild.

months.6: Warm weather makes the coastal trails and marsh boardwalks ideal for easy walking.

chamonix.overview: Chamonix is famous for the multi-day Tour du Mont Blanc and high-altitude day hikes accessed by cable cars and cog railways. Trails in the Aiguilles Rouges offer spectacular views across the valley to the glaciers and peaks of the Mont Blanc massif. The season is strictly dictated by snow, with high routes and lifts operating from June to mid-September.

months.9: An excellent month for hiking with cooler air and clear views of the glaciers. Some lifts begin to close late in the month.

months.1: Winter brings cool, crisp air that makes exploring the maritime forests comfortable.
months.12: Cool winter weather provides pleasant conditions for easy walks through the coastal nature reserves.

months.4: Heat builds significantly in the Palenque region, making lowland walking hard going, while the highlands offer a cooler escape.

chiapas.overview: Chiapas offers walking through dense rainforests, highland pine forests, and around ancient Maya ruins. Trails range from short paths along the turquoise cascades of El Chiflón and the lakes of Montebello to deeper day hikes into the Lacandon Jungle, taken with a local guide. The dry months from November to April provide the best conditions, avoiding the heavy mud and intense humidity of the summer wet season.

chilean-lake-district.overview: The Chilean Lake District offers day hikes through ancient araucaria (monkey puzzle) forests to glacier-fed lakes and volcanic craters. The signature route is the guided walk-up of the active Villarrica volcano, earning views into its smoking crater. Lower trails in Huerquehue National Park loop past waterfalls and alpine lagoons, while the region's heavy rainfall means the walking season is strictly tied to the drier months.

months.8: Cold, wet conditions persist with heavy rain and snow at elevation. Walking remains restricted to short, wet valley trails.
months.10: Snowmelt opens more of the mid-elevation trails in Huerquehue. The Villarrica climb may resume on clear days, though snow remains on the upper slopes.
months.12: December brings excellent walking conditions. The full trail network is open, and the Villarrica climb offers clear views over the surrounding lakes and peaks.

colombian-caribbean.overview: The Colombian Caribbean offers deep jungle trekking and coastal paths. The famous route is the Ciudad Perdida trek, a hot, humid trek of four to six days and roughly 30 miles through the Sierra Nevada mountains to ancient ruins, which requires an authorized guide. Day hikers head to Tayrona National Park for trails through the coastal jungle canopy to remote beaches. The dry months from December to April offer the best trail conditions.

months.2: February remains dry, but Tayrona National Park often closes for the month at the request of the indigenous Kogi people, leaving the Ciudad Perdida trek as the main option.
months.3: With Tayrona reopened and the dry weather holding, March is a prime month for both coastal jungle day hikes and the trek to the Lost City.
months.9: September is one of the wettest months, and the Ciudad Perdida trek is closed for the month for maintenance and indigenous ceremonies, severely limiting the walking options.

cornwall.overview: Cornwall is defined by the South West Coast Path, a continuous trail tracing the jagged shoreline; the Padstow to St Ives stretch alone is about 66 miles over six days. Walkers come for dramatic granite cliffs, hidden coves, and sweeping ocean views that can only be reached on foot. The walking ranges from easy headland loops to steep ascents out of deep river valleys, with inland options across the rugged expanse of Bodmin Moor.

costa-rica.overview: Costa Rica's trails lead through cloud forests, past active volcanoes and into dense coastal jungles. Day hikes in the national parks range from the hanging bridges and cloud-forest paths of Monteverde to the volcanic slopes of Arenal. For a serious challenge, the strenuous trek up Cerro Chirripó reaches the country's highest peak, while the remote coastal trails of Corcovado require a guide.

cotswolds.overview: The Cotswolds offer gentle, pastoral walking through rolling hills, sheep pastures, and honey-colored stone villages. Paths follow public footpaths and bridleways across farmland and through ancient woodlands. The 102-mile Cotswold Way, usually walked in 7 to 10 days, is the main long-distance route, running along the western escarpment with views over the Severn Vale, while shorter loops connect historic market towns.

months.11: The weather turns colder and wetter, and the paths across the farmland become muddy again. The walking requires good boots.
months.12: Short days and cold, wet weather make for muddy walking. The focus shifts to short walks ending at a village pub.

croatia.overview: The Dalmatian Coast offers rugged karst mountains rising straight from the Adriatic, with the best walking found in the limestone gorges of Paklenica National Park and the high ridges of Mount Biokovo. Inland, boardwalks weave through the waterfalls of Plitvice Lakes, requiring timed tickets in summer. Most routes are day hikes ranging from easy coastal paths to steep, rocky ascents that demand sturdy footwear.

months.5: This is a prime month for walking the Dalmatian mountains. Clear skies and temperatures in the 70s make for ideal conditions on the steep trails of Mount Biokovo.
months.8: The rocky coastal mountains radiate heat, making steep ascents dangerous in the afternoon. Stick to dawn hikes or the shaded boardwalks of the inland national parks.
months.2: Coastal trails remain cool. The lower gorges of Paklenica are walkable, but the high peaks of Biokovo are often too cold and icy for safe hiking.

death-valley.overview: Death Valley offers surreal desert hiking through colorful badlands, salt flats, and narrow canyons. The best walking is concentrated in the cooler winter months, with popular day hikes like the Golden Canyon loop exploring the eroded hills. In summer, the valley floor becomes dangerously hot, pushing the only viable hiking high up to the long, strenuous climb of Telescope Peak.

months.1: Winter is mild but often rainy. The coastal paths near Porto remain walkable, and inland vineyard tracks have muddy sections after heavy showers.
months.11: Temperatures drop and autumn rains return. The vineyard tracks can become slick, but clear days still offer excellent walking along the river gorges before winter sets in.

dubai.overview: Dubai's hiking is found outside the city in the rugged Hajar Mountains. The Hatta Wadi Hub offers a network of marked trails through rocky valleys, while a drive to Jebel Jais in neighboring Ras Al Khaimah reaches the country's highest peak and cooler air. Walking here is strictly a winter activity, as the barren, rocky terrain is fully exposed to the intense desert sun.

months.6: The extreme summer heat arrives. Trails are dangerously hot, and only a pre-dawn walk on the high ridges of Jebel Jais is realistic.
months.7: Deep summer brings intense, dangerous heat to the mountains. Trails are too hot for hiking this month.
months.8: The mountains remain dangerously hot and exposed. Hiking is effectively shut down.

ecuadorian-andes.overview: The Ecuadorian Andes offer high-altitude walking among glacier-capped volcanoes, deep crater lakes, and cloud forests. Day hikers can explore the paramo grasslands of Cotopaxi National Park or the lake-dotted valleys of Cajas, while trekkers take on the multi-day Quilotoa Loop, roughly 25 miles in three days, between remote Andean villages. The trails often sit above 10,000 feet, making acclimatization essential, and the best volcano views require walking during the drier months.

egypt.overview: Hiking here centers on the rugged desert mountains of the Sinai Peninsula. The most famous route is the steep climb up Mount Sinai, often walked before dawn to watch the sunrise over the jagged peaks. A local Bedouin guide is required for the ascent, which begins at the monastery car park. Beyond the high peaks, shorter walks explore narrow desert gorges like the Colored Canyon.

el-chalten.overview: El Chaltén is Argentina's hiking capital, with trails that lead straight from town into the jagged peaks of the Andes. The best day hikes are the long trek to Laguna de los Tres, with a steep final climb, for a close-up of Mount Fitz Roy, and the slightly easier valley walk to Laguna Torre beneath Cerro Torre. For multi-day hikers, the demanding Huemul Circuit, about 40 miles in four days, crosses high passes and skirts the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. The prime walking window runs from October to April, though the iconic granite spires can hide behind clouds even on clear days.

months.12: Long days and warmer temperatures make for superb hiking conditions across the Fitz Roy massif. The trails are fully open, though hikers must always be prepared for sudden weather changes.

ethiopia.overview: Ethiopia's Simien Mountains offer some of Africa's most dramatic high-altitude trekking, with sheer escarpments and deep gorges. Routes range from three-day treks along the plateau edge to expedition treks up the 14,930-foot Ras Dashen, with gelada baboons grazing beside the high trails. The national park requires an entrance permit, a guide, and a compulsory armed scout.

everglades.overview: Everglades National Park offers flat, easy walking on paved paths and boardwalks rather than rugged trails. The Anhinga Trail and the Shark Valley loop lead into the sawgrass marshes and hardwood hammocks to see alligators and wading birds up close. The dry season is the walking season; summer brings intense heat, flooded paths, and severe mosquitoes.
